summary: The City of Oceanside, California, supports preserving reliable, affordable connectivity for public libraries and opposes any blanket exclusion of urban and suburban libraries under the E-Rate program. The City of Oceanside argues against tying E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes, as libraries serve a broader range of users beyond students, including adults and seniors. The City supports maintaining the statutory distinction between library-owned computers and patron-owned devices and preserving lawful adult access. The City also supports allowing libraries to use locally appropriate digital literacy work and existing internet safety policies, and assessing the implementation cost and eff The City of Oceanside requests the FCC to retain E-Rate support for public libraries and internal networks, evaluate discount changes against library costs and needs, and simplify certifications for applicants without consultants. The City argues these changes would protect program integrity while maintaining public library access.
